text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a practice where developers regularly combine their code changes into a shared repository. Each time someone adds new code, an automated build starts. The system then runs tests to check that everything works correctly. This helps catch issues early, before they become bigger problems. CI pipelines organise these steps, from building the software to testing it and preparing it for release. By using CI, teams can find bugs faster, improve code quality, and deliver updates more reliably. It has become an essential part of modern software development.
